Voceryq is a recombinant plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy that delivers two plasmids (small pieces of DNA originally derived from bacteria) into the body’s cells, one of which contains the genetic instructions for specific HPV proteins and the other an immune response-enhancing molecule called IL-12. The therapy is designed to stimulate the immune system to respond to and attack cells infected by the specific types of HPV that cause RRP (types 6 and 11). Voceryq is administered via intramuscular (IM) injection using the CELLECTRA 5PSP Device, which delivers the dose and facilitates electroporation, a technique which uses brief electrical pulses to temporarily and reversibly create pores in the cell membranes to enable the delivery of Voceryq into the body’s cells. The safety and effectiveness of Voceryq was evaluated in an open-label multicenter clinical trial in 32 adults diagnosed with RRP. Eligible patients had two or more surgeries to remove laryngotracheal papillomas in the 12 months prior to Voceryq treatment, including a scheduled surgery at trial entry. Seven (27%) out of 26 patients who had at least three baseline surgeries did not require any surgery intervention during the first year after treatment.
